title: A graph neural network nominates OSM–OSMR for melanoma immunotherapy, with ex-vivo explant evidence
summary: MIDAS, a multimodal graph-neural-network model, ranked candidate immuno-oncology targets from gene-interaction, patient multi-omic and immune-biology data. In eight stage III/IV melanoma patient-derived explants, researchers blocked OSM–OSMR signalling with an anti-OSM antibody. The paper reports reduced dysfunctional CD8+ T-cell populations and lower CCL4 levels; PTPN22 inhibition did not produce comparable changes in this assay.
ai_technology: MIDAS, a multimodal graph neural network for immuno-oncology target ranking
organization: University College London; The Francis Crick Institute; Royal Marsden NHS Foundation Trust; University College London Hospitals; Royal Holloway, University of London

evidence.tested: The paper reports reduced dysfunctional CD8+ T-cell populations and lower CCL4 levels; PTPN22 inhibition did not produce comparable changes in this assay.
evidence.unknown: Functional follow-up used only eight stage III/IV melanoma patient-derived explants. This is an ex-vivo preclinical result, not treatment of patients or evidence of clinical benefit. OSM–OSMR biology has prior literature in other tumour settings; the new paper-specific contribution is MIDAS target nomination and measured perturbation effects in melanoma explants. Do not generalize to other cancers or claim a validated therapy.
evidence.ai_role: MIDAS integrated gene-interaction networks with patient multi-omics, immune-cell biology and genetic-perturbation evidence to rank candidate immunotherapy targets. Researchers selected OSM–OSMR for functional follow-up and tested pathway blockade in patient-derived tumour explants; the model nominated the target, while the ex-vivo experiments measured the T-cell and cytokine outcomes.
